subject: Life Skills
title: Handling Defensiveness in Others
description: One-minute skill: Handling Defensiveness in Others.

hook.text: When someone gets defensive, the natural instinct is to push harder. That is exactly the wrong move.

buildup.text: Defensiveness is a fear response. The person feels their identity or competence is under attack.

discovery.text: De-escalation means acknowledging their perspective first. Validation lowers defenses faster than logic.

twist.text: Validation doesn't mean agreement. 'I understand why you'd see it that way' validates without conceding.

climax.text: Validate, then redirect: 'I get that. And here's what I'm also noticing.' Both truths coexist.

punchline.text: Validate first. Then they can hear you.

quiz.question: Why does validation help when someone is defensive?
options: It makes them feel they've won the argument
It lowers their fear response so they can listen
It avoids the real issue entirely
